observations: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show the same electronic keyboard wrapped in clear plastic film, standing upright against a wall/doorway.
Keyboard has a full-size key bed with black and white keys, a small LCD display, a row of buttons, and a speaker grille on the left side.
No clear, legible brand or model text is visible in either photo due to the plastic wrap glare and image resolution.
No power cable, adapter, or power-on indicator is visible in either photo.
Background shows an indoor/outdoor threshold with tiled floor and a person's bare feet, consistent with a casual resale setting, not a studio or verified shop.
A watermark 'MARY OLUGBAMI POSTED ON...' appears on both images, suggesting these are reused/stock seller photos rather than fresh verification shots.

claims.claim: Quality London used keyboard with super sounds
claims.evidence: No audio sample or video provided; sound quality cannot be judged from static photos.
No power-on test, video, or close-up of a key press is shown; keyboard is static and wrapped.
No adapter/power cable visible in either photo.
Requires audio/video test; not shown in photos.
No shipping label, UK plug, or import documentation visible.

risks.risk: Keyboard may not power on or may have dead/unresponsive keys.
risks.proof: A video of the seller powering it on and pressing keys across the full range, with audible sound.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / functionality unverified

risks.risk: Adapter claimed but not shown; could be missing or wrong voltage/plug type.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the adapter next to the keyboard, including plug type.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if adapter not included

risks.risk: Cosmetic damage or cracks hidden under the plastic wrap.
risks.proof: Close-up photos with the plastic wrap removed, especially corners and speaker grille.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic condition unknown/worst case

risks.risk: Brand/model unverifiable, so true market segment and feature set (e.g., number of voices, pitch bend, USB/MIDI) unknown.
risks.proof: A clear, well-lit photo of the brand/model nameplate or screen showing model name.

risks.risk: Speaker or sound quality could be poor despite 'super sounds' claim.
risks.proof: A short video clip playing a demo song or scale through the built-in speakers.

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powering on and playing a scale/demo through its speakers.
Clear photo of the brand/model nameplate or display screen with wrap removed.
Photo of the adapter/power cable alongside the unit.
Close-up photos of corners, keys, and speaker grille without plastic wrap to check for cracks or scratches.
response.reason: The item is clearly a generic 61-key portable electronic keyboard, but brand/model cannot be read from the photos and none of the seller's functional claims (working keys, sound quality, adapter) are verifiable from static wrapped images, so it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, possibly non-working generic keyboard.
